questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using the **BODMAS rule** by handling the **Bracket** and **Multiplication** first.

Bracket: (29 + 21) = 50

Multiplication: 36 × 2 = 72

Expression becomes: 87 − 43 + 68 − 50 + 72

Group positive and negative terms: (87 + 68 + 72) − (43 + 50) = 227 − 93 = 134

**∴ The correct answer is 134.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 87 − 43 + 68 − (29 + 21) + 36 × 2

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 87 − 43 + 68 − 50 + 36 × 2 (Solving **Bracket**)

⇒ 87 − 43 + 68 − 50 + 72 (Solving **Multiplication**)

⇒ 155 − 43 − 50 + 72 (Left to right **Addition/Subtraction**)

⇒ 112 − 50 + 72

⇒ 62 + 72

⇒ 134

**∴ The correct answer is 134.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the **order of operations** to solve mathematical expressions: Brackets (), Of, Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Priority levels

Division and Multiplication share the same priority level and are solved from **left to right**. Addition and Subtraction also share the same priority and are solved similarly.

Bracket sequence

Solve nested brackets in the order: **Circular Brackets** (), then **Curly Brackets** {}, and finally **Square Brackets** [].

questions.question: Evaluate: {{[(6 + 2) × (5 − 3)] + [(12 ÷ 4) × (7 − 2)]} ÷ [(9 − 3) × (2 + 1)]}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the inner parentheses: (8 × 2) and (3 × 5) and (6 × 3).

Numerator value = 16 + 15 = 31.

Denominator value = 6 × 3 = 18.

Final expression = 31 ÷ 18 = 31/18.

**∴ The correct answer is 31/18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** {{[(6 + 2) × (5 − 3)] + [(12 ÷ 4) × (7 − 2)]} ÷ [(9 − 3) × (2 + 1)]}

Following the **BODMAS** rule (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ {{[8 × 2] + [3 × 5]} ÷ [6 × 3]}

⇒ {16 + 15} ÷ 18

⇒ 31 ÷ 18

⇒ 31/18

**∴ The correct answer is 31/18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

This rule dictates the **order of operations** to ensure correct results: **B**rackets first, followed by **O**rders (exponents/roots), then **D**ivision and **M**ultiplication, and finally **A**ddition and **S**ubtraction.

Types of Brackets

When multiple brackets are present, the sequence of solving is: 1) **Parentheses** (), 2) **Curly braces** {}, and 3) **Square brackets** [].

Fraction Representation

A division like a ÷ b is often represented as a **numerator** (a) over a **denominator** (b), resulting in the fraction a/b.

questions.question: Which of the following is greater than (9/16)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **greater fraction**, convert the given values into **decimals**.

Target value: 9 ÷ 16 = 0.5625

Comparing **Option 2**: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625

Since 0.625 > 0.5625, the fraction 5/8 is **greater** than 9/16.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Main fraction = 9/16

**Method:** **Decimal Comparison** or **Cross-Multiplication**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9181b57ea97194800a911779d715ec210a7dfd61803f47c5a9fbf320c28ffb36.png] 

Convert all options to **decimal equivalents** for comparison:

⇒ Target: 9 ÷ 16 = 0.5625

⇒ Option (1): 11 ÷ 20 = 0.5500

⇒ Option (2): 5 ÷ 8 = 0.6250

⇒ Option (3): 27 ÷ 50 = 0.5400

⇒ Option (4): 13 ÷ 32 = 0.40625

⇒ Comparing the results: 0.6250 > 0.5625

⇒ 5/8 > 9/16

**∴ The correct answer is 5/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare two fractions a/b and c/d, check (a × d) and (b × c). If (a × d) > (b × c), then a c/d.

Common Denominator Method

Convert all fractions to have the same **LCM** as the denominator. The fraction with the largest **numerator** is the largest fraction.

Decimal Conversion

Divide the numerator by the denominator to get the **decimal value**, which is the easiest way to compare multiple values quickly.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all fractions to **decimals** for the fastest comparison:

11/5 = 2.20

2 1/4 = 9/4 = 2.25

13/6 = 2.166...

21/10 = 2.10

Comparing the values: 2.10 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Fractions are 11/5, 2 1/4, 13/6, and 21/10.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77e0f19fdc586e61edfac2d10fabfe4a888dc8835f17231548a30f29ae6fd22f.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ First term = 11/5 = 2.2

⇒ Second term = 2 1/4 = 9/4 = 2.25

⇒ Third term = 13/6 = 2.166...

⇒ Fourth term = 21/10 = 2.1

⇒ Arranging in **ascending order**: 2.1 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Comparison by LCM

To compare fractions, find the **LCM** of all denominators and convert them into **like fractions**. The fraction with the smallest numerator is the smallest.

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare a/b and c/d, check the products (a × d) and (b × c). If (a × d) < (b × c), then a/b < c/d.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A **proper fraction** (numerator < denominator) is always smaller than an **improper fraction** (numerator ≥ denominator).

questions.question: A square park has sides of length 9 cm. A, 0.5 cm wide path is inside it. What is the area (in square cm) of the path?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **square park** of side **a** with an **inner path** of width **w**:

**Area of path** = 4w(a − w)

Given: side (a) = 9 cm, width (w) = 0.5 cm

Area = 4 × 0.5 × (9 − 0.5) = 2 × 8.5 = 17 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the **square park** (Outer) = 9 cm

Width of the **path** = 0.5 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f1d17e6a611e3bcd6ad411d002b6906df66eaec8528c14e132f2aef1ea4a2f7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of square = (side)²

Area of path = Area of **outer square** − Area of **inner square**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of **outer square** = 9 × 9 = 81 cm²

⇒ Side of the **inner square** = Outer side − (2 × width)

⇒ Inner side = 9 − (2 × 0.5) = 9 − 1 = 8 cm

⇒ Area of **inner square** = 8 × 8 = 64 cm²

⇒ Area of the **path** = 81 − 64 = 17 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Outer Path Area

When the path is built **outside** the square park, the area is given by 4w(a + w), where 'a' is the side and 'w' is the width.

Cross Path Area

For paths crossing at the center of a rectangle, the area is w(L + B − w), where L is length, B is breadth, and w is path width.

Rectangular Path (Inner)

Area of an **inner path** in a rectangle = 2w(L + B − 2w).

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 54 square cm. The length of the rectangle is 9 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of length and breadth of the rectangle?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Breadth** = **Area** ÷ **Length** = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 cm. **Sum** of **Length** and **Breadth** = 9 + 6 = 15 cm. **∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

questions.question: ((82.5)² - (69.5)²)/(26) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Algebraic Identity**: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Here, a = 82.5 and b = 69.5.

Sum = 82.5 + 69.5 = **152**.

Difference = 82.5 − 69.5 = **13**.

Expression becomes: (152 × 13) ÷ 26 = 152 ÷ 2 = **76**.

**∴ The correct answer is 76.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ((82.5)² − (69.5)²) ÷ 26

**Formula Used:** a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

⇒ ((82.5 + 69.5) × (82.5 − 69.5)) ÷ 26

⇒ (152 × 13) ÷ 26

⇒ 152 × (13 ÷ 26)

⇒ 152 × (1/2)

⇒ 76

**∴ The correct answer is 76.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Two Squares

The identity a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) is essential for simplifying expressions involving the subtraction of two squared terms without calculating the actual squares.

BODMAS Rule

Always solve operations in the order: Brackets, Orders (powers), Division/Multiplication, and Addition/Subtraction to ensure mathematical accuracy.

Simplification Shortcut

When dividing a product (X × Y) ÷ Z, check if Y is a divisor of Z (or vice versa) to reduce the calculation steps early.

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 30. Each number is multiplied by C. New average of these 8 numbers is 120. What is the value of C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each number in a dataset is **multiplied** by a constant **C**, the **Average** of the dataset is also **multiplied** by the same constant **C**.

New Average = Old Average × **C**

120 = 30 × **C**

**C** = 120 ÷ 30 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n) = 8

Initial **Average** = 30

New **Average** = 120

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72920daf7a96750a50d58ab4df9d0113b8894d40bbdfc62e08d320d3c3be34f5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original **Sum** of 8 numbers = Average × Count

⇒ Original **Sum** = 30 × 8 = 240

⇒ When each number is multiplied by **C**, the new sum becomes **C** times the old sum.

⇒ New **Sum** = 120 × 8 = 960

⇒ New **Sum** = Original **Sum** × **C**

⇒ 960 = 240 × **C**

⇒ **C** = 960 ÷ 240

⇒ **C** = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Addition/Subtraction on Average

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every term in a set, the **new average** will be **Old Average ± k**.

Effect of Division on Average

If every number in a set is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the **new average** becomes **Old Average ÷ k**.

Average Property of Linearity

The **Mean** is a linear operator. For any transformation y = ax + b, the **New Mean** = a × (Old Mean) + b.

questions.question: Average of 35 observations is 52. Average of first 14 observations is 54. Average of last 22 observations is 54. What is the value of 14th observation?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Overall **Average** of 35 observations = 52

Total deviation of first 14 (Avg 54) = 14 × (54 − 52) = +28

Total deviation of last 22 (Avg 54) = 22 × (54 − 52) = +44

Since the 14th observation is **repeated**, its value = Average + Total Deviation = 52 + 28 + 44 = 124

**∴ The correct answer is 124.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total observations = 35 | **Average** = 52

First 14 observations **average** = 54

Last 22 observations **average** = 54

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = **Average** × Number of observations

Value of **overlapping observation** = (Sum of Part 1 + Sum of Part 2) − Total Sum

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/323621aa4736703dfcb2a7541ce6a571c1ff2e73b2d5f3abb92b3b6bcdb91b62.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Sum** of 35 observations = 35 × 52 = 1820

⇒ **Sum** of first 14 observations = 14 × 54 = 756

⇒ **Sum** of last 22 observations = 22 × 54 = 1188

⇒ Total sum of subsets (including 14th twice) = 756 + 1188 = 1944

⇒ Value of 14th observation = 1944 − 1820 = 124

**∴ The correct answer is 124.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

In cases of **overlap**, the value of the repeated item is the sum of the base **average** and the net **deviation** of all subsets from that average.

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the individual average.

Exclusion Case

If a number is **excluded**, the value of the excluded observation = (Old Total Sum) − (New Total Sum).

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 9 and their Highest Common Factor is 7. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **sum** of two numbers is equal to the **(sum of ratio parts) × HCF**.

Given **ratio** = 7 : 9 and **HCF** = 7.

Sum = (7 + 9) × 7

Sum = 16 × 7 = 112

**∴ The correct answer is 112.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of two numbers = 7 : 9

**Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10b1cd477fe245cd519b2f7914cf177730189bd5cb127dea0cd68b5ecb7bb767.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 7x and 9x.

⇒ Since 7 and 9 are **co-prime** numbers, their **HCF** is x.

⇒ x = 7 (Given)

⇒ The numbers are (7 × 7) and (9 × 7), which are 49 and 63.

⇒ Sum = 49 + 63

⇒ Sum = 112

**∴ The correct answer is 112.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers A and B, Product of A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

LCM in terms of HCF

If two numbers are in ratio a : b and their HCF is x, then their **LCM** = a × b × x.

Difference of Numbers

The difference of two numbers in ratio a : b (where a > b) is given by (a − b) × HCF.

questions.question: 5 kg of water is mixed in 20 kg of milk. What is the percentage of water in the mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Water** : **Milk** = 5 : 20 = 1 : 4.

Total parts in **mixture** = 1 + 4 = 5 units.

**Water percentage** = (Water part ÷ Total parts) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weight of **water** = 5 kg

Weight of **milk** = 20 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd8b011bb5b528eb660719c0fede64d8283641045d984797f12de7d534ddeab5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Percentage of component = (Quantity of component ÷ Total quantity) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total weight** of mixture = Weight of milk + Weight of water

⇒ Total weight = 20 kg + 5 kg = 25 kg

⇒ **Percentage of water** = (5 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Water % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100

⇒ Water % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Composition

It represents the relative amount of each component in a **mixture** or compound. Sum of percentages of all components always equals 100%.

Mixture Ratios

If component A and B are mixed in ratio x : y, the percentage of A is [x ÷ (x + y)] × 100.

Concentration

In solutions, concentration is often measured as mass-by-mass percentage: (Mass of solute ÷ Mass of solution) × 100.

questions.question: Selling price and cost price of an article is Rs. 3000 and Rs. 4500 respectively. What is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 4500 : 3000 = 3 : 2.

Loss in units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

**Loss Percentage** = (Loss units ÷ CP units) × 100 = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33.33%.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** = ₹4500

**Selling Price (SP)** = ₹3000

**Formula Used:**

Loss = **Cost Price** − **Selling Price**

**Loss Percentage** = (Loss ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/560bbf3962a3b5259f10477838d79f74280a833e610aedfe561bda7bfc17304d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Loss = ₹4500 − ₹3000

⇒ Loss = ₹1500

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (1500 ÷ 4500) × 100

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (1 ÷ 3) × 100

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = 33.333...

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

When SP > CP, Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Relation between SP and CP

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100 OR SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Cost Price Base Rule

Unless specified otherwise, **Profit** and **Loss percentage** are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**.

questions.question: If 30 percent of 1000 is 20 percent more than A, then what is the value of A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate **30% of 1000** = 300.

Since 300 is **20% more** than A, it represents 120% of A.

**A** = (300 ÷ 120) × 100 = 250.

**∴ The correct answer is 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 30% of 1000 is 20% more than A.

**Formula:** Final Value = Base Value × (1 + Increase%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ea90e1b6ef91dffb2c15e16277248eab2c51a54c2888d39a69de27801a70b41.png] 
⇒ **30% of 1000** = (30 ÷ 100) × 1000 = 300 ⇒ Let the value of **A** be the base. ⇒ According to the condition: 300 = A + 20% of A ⇒ 300 = A + 0.20A ⇒ 300 = 1.20A ⇒ A = 300 ÷ 1.20 ⇒ A = 250

**∴ The correct answer is 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

To increase a number **A** by **x%**, the new value is calculated as A × (1 + x ÷ 100).

Finding the Original Value

If a result **R** is **x% more** than **A**, then the original value **A = R ÷ (1 + x ÷ 100)**.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

A 20% increase is equivalent to multiplying the base by the fraction **6/5** or the decimal **1.2**.

questions.question: The profit earned on selling an article for Rs. 1200 is 29 times of the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 600. What is the profit percentage on this article at the selling price of Rs. 1200?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit : Loss** = 29 : 1.

Total ratio parts = 29 + 1 = 30 units.

Difference between **Selling Prices** = 1200 − 600 = ₹600.

30 units = 600 ⇒ 1 unit (Loss) = ₹20.

**Cost Price (CP)** = 600 + 20 = ₹620.

**Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (580 ÷ 620) × 100 = 93.55%.

**∴ The correct answer is 93.55 percent.**

questions.question: A alone can complete 40 percent part of a work in 24 days. A alone will complete 75 percent part of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Since the person **A** is the same, **Time taken** is **directly proportional** to the **Work done**. 40% of work → 24 days 1% of work → 24 ÷ 40 days 75% of work → (24 ÷ 40) × 75 → 0.6 × 75 = 45 days **∴ The correct answer is 45 days.**

questions.question: A is two times efficient as B. A and B together started a work. A left the work after 3 days from starting. B left the work after 6 days from starting. What is the ratio of total work done by A to the total work done by B?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Ratio of **Efficiency** (A : B) = 2 : 1 Ratio of **Time** (A : B) = 3 : 6 = 1 : 2 Ratio of **Work Done** = (Efficiency Ratio) × (Time Ratio) Work Ratio = (2 × 1) : (1 × 2) = 2 : 2 = 1 : 1 **∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

questions.question: Total length of train A and train B is 700 metres. These trains are running in opposite direction. Total speed of train A and train B is 70 m/s. In how much time (in seconds) these trains will cross each other?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two trains cross each other in the **opposite direction**, the **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = 70 m/s (Given as the total speed).

**Total Distance** = Sum of lengths of Train A and Train B = 700 m.

**Time taken** = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 700 ÷ 70 = 10 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of lengths of **Train A** and **Train B** (LA + LB) = 700 m

Sum of speeds (VA + VB) = 70 m/s

Direction = **Opposite**

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross each other = (Total Distance) ÷ (Relative Speed)

In **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = VA + VB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c332500369f5fb210b30105648969bd55e32230806a043b91f81302b0e03ca4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = VA + VB = 70 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = LA + LB = 700 m

⇒ Time = 700 ÷ 70

⇒ Time = 10 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 10 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Rules

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = |V₁ − V₂|. In **opposite directions**, relative speed = V₁ + V₂.

Crossing Different Objects

To cross a **pole or man**, a train covers distance equal to its **own length**. To cross a **platform or bridge**, it covers (Length of train + Length of platform).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: The speed of stream is 4 km/hr. A boat goes 80 km upstream and comes back to the starting point in 15 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use **Option Substitution** in the total time equation: Total Time = D / (u − v) + D / (u + v).

Substitute **v = 4**, **D = 80**, and **Total Time = 15**.

Test **u = 12**: 80 / (12 − 4) + 80 / (12 + 4) = 80 / 8 + 80 / 16 = 10 + 5 = 15 hours.

Since the sum matches the given **15 hours**, 12 is the correct value.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of stream (v) = 4 km/hr

Total distance (one way) = 80 km

Total time taken = 15 hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = u − v | Downstream Speed = u + v (where u is boat speed in still water)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7cde8ad9fdb1b4f75cffb4db8b81b80e5943b1c224e9bc712ad13cf3a8df204b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 80 / (u − 4) + 80 / (u + 4) = 15

⇒ 80 × [(u + 4 + u − 4) / (u² − 16)] = 15

⇒ 80 × [2u / (u² − 16)] = 15

⇒ 160u = 15(u² − 16)

⇒ 32u = 3(u² − 16)

⇒ 3u² − 32u − 48 = 0

⇒ 3u² − 36u + 4u − 48 = 0

⇒ 3u(u − 12) + 4(u − 12) = 0

⇒ (3u + 4)(u − 12) = 0

⇒ u = 12 (as speed cannot be negative)

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream speed (D) = u + v and Upstream speed (U) = u − v. Consequently, boat speed u = (D + U) / 2 and stream speed v = (D − U) / 2.

Average Speed of Boat

For a round trip between two points, the average speed of the boat is given by (u² − v²) / u.

Ratio of Speeds

If the time taken to go downstream and upstream is t₁ and t₂ respectively, then u / v = (t₂ + t₁) / (t₂ − t₁).

questions.question: The cost price of an article is Rs. 15000. It is sold at a profit of 20 percent. A discount of 25 percent was given. What is the marked price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct ratio between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 25) : (100 + 20) = 75 : 120

Simplifying the ratio: 75 : 120 → 5 : 8

Given 5 units = ₹15000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹3000

8 units = 8 × 3000 = ₹24000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] <span style="vertical-align: middle;font-size: 21px;"

questions.question: Total marked price of 20 articles is Rs. 300. 40 percent discount is given. How many articles can be purchased for Rs. 45? (marked price of each article is same)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Marked Price (MP)** of 1 article = 300 ÷ 20 = ₹15.

**Selling Price (SP)** after 40% **discount** = 60% of 15 = ₹9.

**Number of articles** for ₹45 = 45 ÷ 9 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 articles.**
